texts: good. the copular clause with a date on it reifies the full-moon state, keeps the flat past copular atom beside it, and hangs both date terms on the state, so both "was the moon full?" and "when?" resolve. One soft spot you cannot write around: an epoch date like "day 21 of Year 1" has no dedicated calendar term, so it lands on (Day 21) + (Year 1) where (Day n) elsewhere means day-of-month — nothing is lost, and no rewrite of the date parses better.

good. one past convene event with the Council as agent and "at the Watch" as its location, both capitalized labels typed as ordinary referents (a bare kind-word label gets no name atom, which is the intended handling).

good. one past redistribute event with the Council as agent and mire-essence as what was moved, "across the lantern-stations" kept on the surface preposition over a group of those stations, and both compounds unpacked to their genus (mire-essence is an essence, a lantern-station is a station).

good. the Northcove stations come out as a group with their link to Northcove recorded, the central pool as one typed individual that the next sentence reuses, and the contributing is carried both by the group and by a fireable per-member rule, so a station named later inherits its own contribution.

good. every participant is covered — the extra mire-essence as its own witness carrying "extra", the Middle Row stations as a group linked to the named Middle Row, and the same central pool reused as the source — with the issue event tying them together in the past.

mixed: the record event, its Council agent, and the back-reference to the earlier redistribution are all right, but "in the Watch ledgers" is read as the place where the recording happened — the parse says the Council was inside the books rather than that the books are what the record went into. Rewrite as "The Council wrote the redistribution into the ledgers of the Watch." — "into" marks the ledgers as the destination of the writing instead of a location, and the of-phrase states the Watch link outright rather than leaving a capitalized premodifier to be guessed at.
